basis: Birmingham is a current confirmed employee-earnings occupational-tax positive; no complete current statewide adopter registry was found.
The current Alaska Taxable report is officially described as covering all municipalities and every tax type; it reports no in-scope municipal tax.
Current statute preempts local income taxation while the urban revenue-sharing fund is maintained.
Act 96 of 2023 prohibits local governments from levying an income tax and repealed prior local authority.
State sources regulate a local earnings tax if otherwise authorized, but current charter/general-law authority and the adopter universe were not closed.
Denver's employee occupational privilege tax is flat rather than compensation-calculated; no complete statewide source was found for the broader requested class.
The General Assembly's statewide municipal-finance analysis says municipalities can levy only property taxes; current employee withholding is State income tax.
The statute limits municipal earned-income taxing authority to municipalities over 50,000; the current official population source leaves Wilmington as the sole qualifying municipality.
The state constitution prohibits a natural-person income tax by the state or under its authority beyond now-unavailable federal credits.

O.C.G.A. section 48-7-140 categorically prohibits political subdivisions from levying or collecting local income taxes; business gross-receipts occupation taxes are outside the employee-wage definition.
The State says Hawaii has no independent or separate cities or other municipalities; counties and quasi-county Kalawao are outside this municipal audit.
Municipal taxing power requires legislative investment; the research did not conclusively prove that no compensation-tax authorization exists elsewhere.
The current 2026 legislative tax handbook states that no local personal-income tax is authorized, including for home-rule units without statutory authorization.
Current local income tax is county-based; municipal authority begins in fiscal year 2028 and requires a mandatory refresh before then.
Current city-finance taxes are property-based and the located local income surtax is county-imposed and resident-only, but the home-rule and special-act residual was not conclusively closed.
K.S.A. 12-140 expressly prohibits city income taxes; its local-option intangibles exception does not cover employee wages.
Current official sources confirm local occupational license taxes on wages and net profits, but no demonstrably complete current municipal adopter registry was found.
Louisiana Constitution article VII, section 4(C) prohibits every political subdivision, including municipalities, from levying an income tax.
Current municipal taxation is property-based and income withholding is State-administered, but broad municipal home rule prevents complete special-charter closure.
The state administers the closed universe of 23 county-equivalent local income taxes plus Baltimore City; Baltimore City is the sole municipal-equivalent record.
The Home Rule Amendment does not itself grant local taxing power, but the General Court may grant it; no current wage-tax grant was found and the special-law universe remains open.
Michigan Treasury publishes the current statewide closed list of 24 cities imposing an income tax.
Current statute prohibits local income taxes except under enumerated conditions not establishing a municipal employee wage-tax adopter.
A project-specific Job Development Assessment Fee may be wage-deducted and reported as local tax, but it is nonmunicipal and current legacy-project status is unresolved.
The statutory class is closed and current official sources establish Kansas City and St. Louis as the municipal earnings-tax adopters.
Self-government units cannot authorize an income tax without delegation; no complete current inventory of special delegations was found.
The Nebraska Legislature states that Nebraska has never authorized local income taxes; current individual income tax is State-imposed.
The state constitution prohibits state and local individual income taxes.
The State has no W-2 wage income tax and its current tax universe identifies no municipal wage tax, but special municipal charter authority was not conclusively closed.
Newark and Jersey City payroll taxes are employer-incidence taxes; Jersey City expressly prohibits deduction or withholding from employees, while employee income withholding is State tax.
Municipal income tax is prohibited, including for home-rule municipalities, and the current State-administered municipal local-option program is limited to gross-receipts taxes.
Current state withholding sources close the municipal universe to New York City and Yonkers.
Current statute reserves income taxation and prohibits local income taxes except as expressly authorized; no in-scope exception applies.
Current municipal home-rule provisions do not authorize income taxation and official legislative material confirms the limitation.
Ohio Taxation's Finder provides the authoritative statewide current municipal rate universe and machine-readable downloads; JEDD/JEDZ are separate.
Oklahoma law bars municipal earnings, payroll, or income taxes on nonresidents; any resident-only municipal tax is outside this worksite-and-commuter definition.
Eugene has a confirmed employee payroll tax and Portland has a resident-only income tax; no complete current statewide municipal registry was found.
DCED's statutory statewide Real-Time Register uniquely identifies every municipality/PSD and current EIT/LST data; Philadelphia is a direct overlay outside Act 32.
General city and town levy authority is property-based and income tax is State-administered, but the General Assembly's municipality-specific special-law universe was not exhausted.

The Department of Commerce states there is no local income tax and current law bars new local taxes absent specific authorization; pre-1997 and special-authority occupational-tax possibilities were not completely inventoried.
The official municipal-tax page covers sales/use/gross-receipts taxes but does not prove that those are the exclusive municipal taxes.
The Constitution prohibits state or local tax on payroll or earned personal income but preserves taxes in effect on 2011-01-01; no complete official legacy-tax inventory was found.
Official city-tax sources identify property and sales taxes but do not provide an explicit municipal compensation-tax prohibition or complete all-tax registry.
Current state withholding guidance was found, but no explicit municipal preemption or complete local-tax registry was established.
Current municipal local-option authority enumerates only sales, meals/alcohol, and rooms taxes; the official charter corpus contains no employee-wage grant.
Current code prohibits political subdivisions from taxing payrolls or occupations and prohibits counties, cities, and towns from taxing income.
Current law prohibits counties, cities, and other local governments from taxing individuals on personal income; Seattle's payroll expense tax is employer-only and separate.
Current statute conditionally authorizes a percentage municipal occupational tax on earned income, but no complete current adopter/termination registry was found.
Wisconsin Statutes section 66.0611 expressly voids any political-subdivision tax on or measured by income.
Official local-tax materials located were not an exhaustive all-tax registry and no explicit municipal compensation-tax prohibition was established.
DC is a single district-equivalent jurisdiction with a current resident individual-income-tax and withholding system; it is resident-based and not a company-situs municipal match.
